jobs.occupation: Post-Doc: Agentic AI for Self-Driving Labs in Materials Science (Ingenieur/in - Materialwissenschaften)
jobs.description: Self-driving laboratories are revolutionizing material science these days. They rely on autonomous robotic systems that can massively speed up experimental work. Agentic Artificial Intelligence (Al) is controlling them, for example, by analyzing the data they collect and planning new experiments based on these data.At the Hereon Institute of Surface Science, we study how light metals degrade and how to control that degradation for structural, biomedical and energy storage applications. Our robotic testing platform already screens hundreds of electrolyte additives and will be extended to screen coating formulations, generating data for machine learning. In this project, in strong collaboration with the Hereon Institute of Material System Modeling you will build the AI agents that will screen properties of chemical compounds, design experiments, analyze results in real time, and draw on the literature and on our growing databases to decide what to try next. You will work hand in hand with experimental researchers, focused on degradation control. Their laboratories will be the proving ground for your agents. Join us to build a self-driving laboratory of corrosion science.We are offering a 3-year position, as soon as possible, as a Postdoc in the quickly developing field of agentic AI for materials science. The position is full-time (39 h/week) and will be located in Hereon's main campus, in Geesthacht (near Hamburg).Equal opportunity is an important part of our personnel policy. We would therefore strongly encourage qualified women to apply for the position.Your tasks:- design and implement AI agents that plan, execute and evaluate experiments on our robotic testing platform- integrate the agents with our laboratory equipment and IT infrastructure, including electronic lab notebooks and databases, to enable closed-loop experimentation- develop decision-making strategies that combine large language models (LLMs) with active learning and Bayesian optimization, so that promising compounds, coating formulations and testing conditions are identified with as few experiments as possible- work side by side with experimental scientists and translate their scientific questions into autonomous workflows that accelerate their research- build tools that extract knowledge from scientific literature and from our own datasets, turning them into machine-readable, FAIR resources- publish your results in leading journals, present at international conferences, write project reports and contribute to open-source software and open datasetsYour profile:- a completed Master's and PhD degree in computational materials science, computational engineering, computer science, data science, chemistry, physics or a related field- strong programming skills in Python and hands-on experience with large language models (LLMs), agent frameworks, or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)- experience with machine learning (ideally also active learning or Bayesian optimization)- experience with robotics, instrument control, APls, databases or software engineering- genuine interest in laboratory automation and in applying AI to real scientific problems- basic knowledge of chemistry, electrochemistry and materials science- enjoying teamwork and clear communication across disciplines, particularly with experimental researchers- very good English, knowledge of the German language is preferred but not mandatory, we support language learningOur offer:- an exciting and varied job in a research center with around 1,000 employees from more than 60 nations- an International Welcome Office with guest accommodation- 6 weeks holiday per year; company holidays between Christmas and New Year's Day- social benefits under the collective agreement for the German public sector and remuneration up to pay grade 13 (EntgO Bund)- very good work-life balance; options for mobile and flexible working- cooperation with Hamburg University of Technology, TUHH, our partner university- access to state-of-the-art (robotic) labs, unique scientific and technical infrastructure- access to a large international research and industrial network- funding for conferences, summer schools and courses needed or research stays- a well-connected research campus, good networking opportunities, a subsidized Deutschlandticket Job ticket) subject to certain conditions, and charging facilities for electric vehicles- a family-friendly working environment
